partnershipPlan: Two carer representatives from the carers' forum review the exposure definition and the plain-language summary; ward discharge coordinators advise on how meetings are recorded; the medical director's office receives interim reports only on progress, not results.
socialListening: No social media listening; anonymised compliments and complaints about discharge from the patient advice service in the last year are read for mentions of family meetings.

items.theme: Hearing about the meeting too late
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: They rang on the Tuesday morning to say the meeting was at eleven; I was at work two towns away.
items.implication: Record how much notice families were given and whether telephone joining was offered.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: The meeting only helped because we left with a sheet saying who was coming each morning and who to ring.
items.implication: Keep the written plan in the exposure definition.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Everyone decided what would happen to me and nobody asked what I could still do myself.
items.implication: Note whether the patient took part in the meeting as a descriptive variable.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I book meetings for the families I am worried about; the easy ones go home without one.
items.implication: Treat complexity as the main confounder and analyse unattended bookings separately.

summary: Four composite voices on notice, written plans, patient participation and how meetings are chosen.
